amendments.rule: Read `בֵּין X וּבֵין Y` by the connective the ASV actually writes. Where it is recast as *X from Y*, the second `בֵּין` carries *from*, while the first `בֵּין` and its waw are `unrepresented`. Where the ASV preserves *between X and Y*, the first `בֵּין` takes *between*, the waw takes *and*, and the repeated second `בֵּין` is `unrepresented`. Do not transfer the *and* to the repeated preposition: the waw is the morpheme that licenses it. **A verse may write more than one such pair, and the count runs pair by pair.** Where the ASV writes a *between* for each pair — `בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ וּבֵין הַחֹל וּבֵין הַטָּמֵא וּבֵין הַטָּהוֹר` → *between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean* — each written *between* belongs to the `בֵּין` that opens the pair it stands before, only the `בֵּין` repeated inside a pair is `unrepresented`, and every waw keeps the *and* written for it. Do not read *the repeated second `בֵּין`* above as every `בֵּין` after the first in the phrase: count the ASV's *between*s against the pairs and read which pair each opens, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s. **Hebrew also writes the second member with `לְ` in place of a repeated `בֵּין`, and the same reading follows the morpheme that is actually there.** In `בֵּין X לְ Y` → *between X and Y* the `בֵּין` takes *between* and the `לְ` takes the *and*, exactly as the waw does above, because the `לְ` is what stands where the connective stands and no waw is present to claim it: `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה` → *between sheep and sheep* is the shape. Do not mark such a `לְ` `unrepresented` in order to leave the *and* `added`, and do not reach for rule 14's last sentence: that sentence governs a connective no morpheme answers to, and here one does. **Where the phrase runs on into further `לְ` members the ASV writes as bare coordinated nouns, only the `לְ` standing where the ASV writes its connective takes one.** `בֵּין שֶׂה לָשֶׂה לָאֵילִים וְלָעַתּוּדִים` → *between sheep and sheep, the rams and the he goats* gives *and* to the first `לְ`, leaves the two later ones `unrepresented` under rule 40, and gives the second written *and* to the waw. Count the phrase's connective morphemes against the ASV's connectives and read which pair of members each stands between, as rule 42 counts waws against *and*s.
amendments.why: Rule 26's third sentence speaks of 'the repeated second בֵּין', which is exact for a single pair but can be read as marking every בֵּין after the first unrepresented. LEV.10.10 writes four בֵּין in two coordinated pairs and the ASV writes a *between* for each pair; the verse gave each written *between* to the בֵּין opening its own pair and left the two repeated ones unrepresented, each waw keeping its *and*. The amendment states that count for בֵּין in the rule's own terms, exactly as its closing sentence already states it for the לְ members, so the extension introduces no principle the rule did not already hold and contradicts no corpus treatment. Everything else in the rule is preserved verbatim.

conventions: A possessive or belonging לְ standing in the predicate of הָיָה לְ fuses with the English possessive or genitive word that carries both the relation and the possessor's lexeme (rule 49's closing clause), and is not marked unrepresented under rule 40. LEV.10.15 aligns לְךָ → thine headed on the suffix and לְבָנֶיךָ → sons' headed on the noun, the suffix keeping its own thy; coordinated members of one predicate are read alike.

Sacrificial nouns the ASV renders by an English offering phrase keep the generic word offering(s) inside the source noun's own unit and head on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 31): חַטָּאת → sin offering on sin (vv. 16, 17, 19), עֹלָה → burnt offering on burnt (v. 19), מִנְחָה → meal offering on meal (v. 12), שֶׁלֶם → peace offerings on peace (v. 14), תְּנוּפָה → wave offering on wave (v. 15). offering is never the head and is never added.

אִשֶּׁה is rendered by the whole phrase the offerings made by fire, headed on fire, with a supplied the joining that unit where no article morpheme stands (vv. 12, 13, 15). In vv. 12 and 13 the unit is discontinuous around of Jehovah, which belongs to the following name under rule 19. The competing head offerings is named in each unit's note.

Qal קָרַב → draw near, drew near heads on near, which carries the lexeme under rule 44's subtraction (vv. 4, 5); the competing head draw is named in each note. Hiphil קָרַב is rendered by the single offered (vv. 1, 19) and raises no head question.
כַּאֲשֶׁר is fused as as under rule 30 and headed on the comparative preposition כְּ (vv. 5, 15, 18); the competing reading heads on the relative אֲשֶׁר and is named in each unit's note.

report: Read all 45 candidate groups and all 20 verse dumps end to end. One genuine split, in LEV.10.15; five chapter-wide judgments recorded; one narrow amendment to rule 26.

The split: LEV.10.15 analysed the two coordinated members of one possessive predicate two ways. The first, לְךָ, was fused into thine under rule 49's closing clause; the coordinated וּלְבָנֶיךָ had its לְ marked unrepresented under rule 40, although the ASV writes that preposition's belonging relation inside the genitive thy sons'. Rule 49 closes on exactly this case (לַיהוָה → is Jehovah's) and forbids splitting the pair on the ground that the noun holds an English word of its own. s024 now shares s025's unit, headed on sons; the suffix keeps its own thy. Partition re-verified: 35 source and 47 target ids used exactly once across 32 units.

Candidates checked and rejected as source- or ASV-licensed: מֵאֵת פְּנֵי → from + before (v.4) against מִלִּפְנֵי → from + before (v.2), each taking the corpus-attested fusion of the second morpheme actually present; אֶל unrepresented before a bare English object in vv.4-5 against unto elsewhere (rule 40); four בֵּין against two written betweens in v.10 (rule 26); אַל → no in v.9 against not in v.6, which rule 15 divides by whether the ASV writes a determiner on a nominal; הַיּוֹם → this day and to day within v.19, both corpus-attested (rules 41, 30); חֹק → as thy portion (v.14, no preposition present, rule 33) against as a portion (v.15, a written לְ); לְ before an infinitive taking that, to, or nothing as the ASV writes.

The candidate table is blind to added units, so the dump was read for supplied English folded into a licensing morpheme. The chapter is consistent: a supplied completion word joins the unit of the morpheme it completes (each of them in v.1, the hair of in v.6, the offerings made by fire in vv.12, 13 and 15, things in v.19), and the one added unit is v.15's object pronoun it, which rule 44 leaves added because no object morpheme stands in the clause.

BSB: all twelve disagreements are documented convention differences — the object marker (rule 16, vv.2, 14, 16), the לְ of לֵאמֹר (rule 27, vv.3, 8, 16), אֶל before a bare English object and the dative לְ of v.17 (rule 40), and the repeated בֵּין of v.10 (rule 26). None is a genuine error. The v.15 patch incidentally removes one of them; it was made on rule 49 grounds and not to move the figure.

Contract: no new rules. Rule 26 is amended because its sentence about 'the repeated second בֵּין' can be read as marking every בֵּין after the first unrepresented, which v.10's two coordinated pairs contradict; the rule's own counting sentence already says otherwise for its לְ members.
